passages.text: “If a man divorces his wife and she leaves him to marry another, can he ever return to her? Would not such a land be completely defiled? But you have played the harlot with many lovers— and you would return to Me?” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
He uses the example of marriage.
If a man divorces his wife, she leaves him.
She marries another man.
Can her first husband return to her?
No, he cannot return to her.
If he did, the land would become completely defiled.
You, My people, have acted like an unfaithful wife.
You have had many lovers.
Yet you want to return to Me.
This is what the LORD declares.
passages.original: לֵאמֹ֡ר הֵ֣ן יְשַׁלַּ֣ח אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ אִשְׁתּוֹ֩ וְהָלְכָ֨ה מֵאִתּ֜וֹ וְהָיְתָ֣ה לְאִישׁ־ אַחֵ֗ר הֲיָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ ע֔וֹד הֲל֛וֹא חָנ֥וֹף תֶּחֱנַ֖ף הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֑יא וְאַ֗תְּ זָנִית֙ רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וְשׁ֥וֹב אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Lift up your eyes to the barren heights and see. Is there any place where you have not been violated? You sat beside the highways waiting for your lovers, like a nomad in the desert. You have defiled the land with your prostitution and wickedness.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God tells them to look up to the barren hills.
God asks them to see what has happened there.
There is no place where they have not been violated.
They sat by the roads and waited for their lovers.
They acted like a nomad in the desert.
They defiled the land.
They did this through their prostitution.
They did this through their wickedness.
passages.original: שְׂאִֽי־ עֵינַ֨יִךְ עַל־ שְׁפָיִ֜ם וּרְאִ֗י אֵיפֹה֙ לֹ֣א שֻׁגַּלְתְּ עַל־ דְּרָכִים֙ יָשַׁ֣בְתְּ לָהֶ֔ם כַּעֲרָבִ֖י בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַתַּחֲנִ֣יפִי אֶ֔רֶץ בִּזְנוּתַ֖יִךְ וּבְרָעָתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Therefore the showers have been withheld, and no spring rains have fallen. Yet you have the brazen look of a prostitute; you refuse to be ashamed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God has withheld the showers.
No spring rains have fallen.
You have the bold face of a prostitute.
You refuse to feel shame.
passages.original: וַיִּמָּנְע֣וּ רְבִבִ֔ים וּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ ל֣וֹא הָיָ֑ה וּמֵ֨צַח אִשָּׁ֤ה זוֹנָה֙ הָ֣יָה לָ֔ךְ מֵאַ֖נְתְּ הִכָּלֵֽם׃

passages.text: Have you not just called to Me, ‘My Father, You are my friend from youth.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God says, “You have called to Me.”
You said, “My Father, You are my friend.”
You said, “You have been my friend since I was young.”
passages.original: הֲל֣וֹא מֵעַ֔תָּה קָרָאתִי לִ֖י אָבִ֑י אַלּ֥וּף נְעֻרַ֖י אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Will He be angry forever? Will He be indignant to the end?’ This you have spoken, but you keep doing all the evil you can.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to His people Israel.
God saw that they sinned and did evil.
God heard them say, “Will He be angry forever?”
They also said, “Will He stay angry to the end?”
God said, “You have spoken these words.”
But you keep doing all the evil you can.
You do not stop your wrong actions.
You continue to sin even after you speak these things.
passages.original: הֲיִנְטֹ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֔ם אִם־ יִשְׁמֹ֖ר לָנֶ֑צַח הִנֵּ֥ה דִבַּרְתִּי וַתַּעֲשִׂ֥י הָרָע֖וֹת וַתּוּכָֽל׃פ

passages.text: Now in the days of King Josiah, the LORD said to me, “Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree to prostitute herself there.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me during the days of King Josiah.
The LORD asked me a question.
He said, “Have you seen what faithless Israel has done?
Israel has acted without faithfulness.
She has gone up on every high hill.
She has gone under every green tree.
She has prostituted herself there.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲ‍ֽרָאִ֔יתָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֹלְכָ֨ה הִ֜יא עַל־ כָּל־ הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַּ וְאֶל־ תַּ֛חַת כָּל־ עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָ֖ן וַתִּזְנִי־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: I thought that after she had done all these things, she would return to Me. But she did not return, and her unfaithful sister Judah saw it.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeremiah during the days of King Josiah.
God saw what faithless Israel did.
Israel sinned in many ways.
God thought Israel would return to Him after all her sins.
Israel did not return to God.
Judah is Israel’s sister.
Judah was also unfaithful.
Judah saw that Israel did not return to God.
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֗ר אַחֲרֵ֨י עֲשׂוֹתָ֧הּ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֵ֛לֶּה אֵלַ֥י תָּשׁ֖וּב וְלֹא־ שָׁ֑בָה וַתֵּרֶאה בָּגוֹדָ֥ה אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: She saw that because faithless Israel had committed adultery, I gave her a certificate of divorce and sent her away. Yet that unfaithful sister Judah had no fear and prostituted herself as well.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me in the days of King Josiah.
The LORD saw that Israel was faithless.
Israel committed adultery against the LORD.
Because of this, the LORD sent Israel away.
The LORD gave Israel a certificate of divorce.
Judah is Israel’s sister.
Judah was also unfaithful.
Judah saw what happened to Israel.
Judah did not fear the LORD.
Judah also prostituted herself.
Judah followed the same sins as Israel.
passages.original: וָאֵ֗רֶא כִּ֤י עַל־ כָּל־ אֹדוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִֽאֲפָה֙ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁלַּחְתִּ֕יהָ וָאֶתֵּ֛ן אֶת־ סֵ֥פֶר כְּרִיתֻתֶ֖יהָ אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֨א יָֽרְאָ֜ה בֹּֽגֵדָ֤ה יְהוּדָה֙ אֲחוֹתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ וַתִּ֥זֶן גַּם־ הִֽיא׃

passages.text: Indifferent to her own infidelity, Israel had defiled the land and committed adultery with stones and trees.
passages.sermon:
Israel acted without shame.
Israel was unfaithful to God.
Israel defiled the land.
Israel committed adultery with stones.
Israel committed adultery with trees.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ מִקֹּ֣ל זְנוּתָ֔הּ וַתֶּחֱנַ֖ף אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַתִּנְאַ֥ף אֶת־ הָאֶ֖בֶן וְאֶת־ הָעֵֽץ׃

passages.text: Yet in spite of all this, her unfaithful sister Judah did not return to Me with all her heart, but only in pretense,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Judah was Israel’s sister.
Judah was unfaithful.
Judah saw what happened to Israel.
Israel was faithless and was sent away.
Yet Judah did not return to Me.
Judah did not come back with all her heart.
Judah only pretended to return.
This is what the LORD says.
passages.original: וְגַם־ בְּכָל־ זֹ֗את לֹא־ שָׁ֨בָה אֵלַ֜י בָּגוֹדָ֧ה אֲחוֹתָ֛הּ יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּכָל־ לִבָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י אִם־ בְּשֶׁ֖קֶר נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than unfaithful Judah.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD compared Israel and Judah.
Israel was faithless.
Judah was unfaithful.
The LORD said Israel showed herself more righteous than Judah.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Go, proclaim this message toward the north: ‘Return, O faithless Israel,’ declares the LORD. ‘I will no longer look on you with anger, for I am merciful,’ declares the LORD. ‘I will not be angry forever.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a command.
The LORD told Jeremiah to go north.
The LORD told Jeremiah to proclaim a message.
The LORD said, “Return, faithless Israel.”
The LORD declared this message.
The LORD said, “I will not look on you with anger.”
The LORD said, “I am merciful.”
The LORD declared, “I will not be angry forever.”
passages.original: הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה לֽוֹא־ אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ חָסִ֤יד אֲנִי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א אֶטּ֖וֹר לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Only acknowledge your guilt, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God. You have scattered your favors to foreign gods under every green tree and have not obeyed My voice,’ ” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Israel.
The LORD is Israel’s God.
The LORD says, “Acknowledge your guilt.
You have rebelled against Me.
You have given your ways to foreign gods.
You did this under every green tree.
You did not listen to My voice.
I, the LORD, declare this.”
passages.original: אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ כִּ֛י בַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖יִךְ פָּשָׁ֑עַתְּ וַתְּפַזְּרִ֨י אֶת־ דְּרָכַ֜יִךְ לַזָּרִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת כָּל־ עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֔ן וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא־ שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Return, O faithless children,” declares the LORD, “for I am your master, and I will take you—one from a city and two from a family—and bring you to Zion.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Israel.
The LORD calls Israel faithless children.
The LORD says, "Return to Me."
The LORD declares, "I am your master."
The LORD promises, "I will take you back."
The LORD says, "I will take one person from a city."
The LORD says, "I will take two people from a family."
The LORD promises, "I will bring you to Zion."
passages.original: שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י בָּעַ֣לְתִּי בָכֶ֑ם וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם אֶחָ֣ד מֵעִ֗יר וּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ מִמִּשְׁפָּחָ֔ה וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking to His people.
The LORD promises to give you new leaders.
These leaders will be shepherds.
These shepherds will have hearts like God's heart.
These shepherds will care for you.
They will feed you with knowledge.
They will feed you with understanding.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֛ם רֹעִ֖ים כְּלִבִּ֑י וְרָע֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם דֵּעָ֥ה וְהַשְׂכֵּֽיל׃

passages.text: “In those days, when you multiply and increase in the land,” declares the LORD, “they will no longer discuss the ark of the covenant of the LORD. It will never come to mind, and no one will remember it or miss it, nor will another one be made.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
He says, “In those days you will grow in number.
You will become many in the land.
You will not talk about the ark of the covenant of the LORD anymore.
No one will think about the ark.
No one will remember the ark.
No one will miss the ark.
No one will make another ark.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֡ה כִּ֣י תִרְבּוּ֩ וּפְרִיתֶ֨ם בָּאָ֜רֶץ בַּיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵ֙מָּה֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה לֹא־ יֹ֣אמְרוּ ע֗וֹד אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִית־ יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־ לֵ֑ב וְלֹ֤א יִזְכְּרוּ־ בוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִפְקֹ֔דוּ וְלֹ֥א יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: At that time Jerusalem will be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations will be gathered in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
passages.sermon:
God will act in the future.
At that time, people will call Jerusalem the Throne of the LORD.
All nations will gather in Jerusalem.
They will come to honor the name of the LORD.
The people will not follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts anymore.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יִקְרְא֤וּ לִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ כִּסֵּ֣א יְהוָ֔ה וְנִקְוּ֨וּ אֵלֶ֧יהָ כָֽל־ הַגּוֹיִ֛ם לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה לִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־ יֵלְכ֣וּ ע֔וֹד אַחֲרֵ֕י שְׁרִר֖וּת לִבָּ֥ם הָרָֽע׃ס

passages.text: In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and they will come together from the land of the north to the land that I gave to your fathers as an inheritance.
passages.sermon:
In those days, the house of Judah and the house of Israel will act together.
They will walk together.
They will come from the land of the north.
They will come to the land I gave to your fathers.
I gave this land to your fathers as an inheritance.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔מָּה יֵלְכ֥וּ בֵית־ יְהוּדָ֖ה עַל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְיָבֹ֤אוּ יַחְדָּו֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן עַל־ הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִנְחַ֖לְתִּי אֶת־ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then I said, ‘How I long to make you My sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of all the nations!’ I thought you would call Me ‘Father’ and never turn away from following Me.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Israel.
God wanted to make Israel His sons.
God wanted to give Israel a good land.
This land was the most beautiful among all nations.
God hoped Israel would call Him Father.
God wanted Israel to stay close to Him.
God did not want Israel to turn away from Him.
passages.original: וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֵ֚יךְ אֲשִׁיתֵ֣ךְ בַּבָּנִ֔ים וְאֶתֶּן־ לָךְ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֔ה נַחֲלַ֥ת צְבִ֖י צִבְא֣וֹת גּוֹיִ֑ם וָאֹמַ֗ר אָבִי֙ תִּקְרְאוּ לִ֔י וּמֵאַחֲרַ֖י לֹ֥א תָשׁוּבוּ׃

passages.text: But as a woman may betray her husband, so you have betrayed Me, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the house of Israel.
The LORD says, “A woman can betray her husband.
You, house of Israel, have betrayed Me in the same way.
I, the LORD, declare this.”
passages.original: אָכֵ֛ן בָּגְדָ֥ה אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵרֵעָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן בְּגַדְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: A voice is heard on the barren heights, the children of Israel weeping and begging for mercy, because they have perverted their ways and forgotten the LORD their God.
passages.sermon:
The children of Israel are the people God chose.
They live in the land God gave them.
A voice comes from the barren hills.
People hear weeping on the heights.
The children of Israel cry out.
They beg for mercy.
They have done wrong.
They have changed their ways for evil.
They have forgotten the LORD.
The LORD is their God.
passages.original: ק֚וֹל עַל־ שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת־ דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת־ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: “Return, O faithless children, and I will heal your faithlessness.” “Here we are. We come to You, for You are the LORD our God.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God calls them His children.
God says they have been faithless.
God tells them to return to Him.
God promises to heal their faithlessness.
The people answer God.
They say, “Here we are.”
They say, “We come to You.”
They say, “You are the LORD our God.”
passages.original: שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים אֶרְפָּ֖ה מְשׁוּבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם הִנְנוּ֙ אָתָ֣נוּ לָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Surely deception comes from the hills, and commotion from the mountains. Surely the salvation of Israel is in the LORD our God.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel look to the hills and mountains.
They find only lies and confusion there.
The hills and mountains cannot save them.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD alone gives salvation to Israel.
passages.original: אָכֵ֥ן לַשֶּׁ֛קֶר מִגְּבָע֖וֹת הָמ֣וֹן הָרִ֑ים אָכֵן֙ בַּיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ תְּשׁוּעַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: From our youth, that shameful god has consumed what our fathers have worked for— their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.
passages.sermon:
Shame is a false god.
Shame has taken what our fathers worked for.
Shame has done this since our youth.
Shame has consumed their flocks.
Shame has consumed their herds.
Shame has consumed their sons.
Shame has consumed their daughters.
passages.original: וְהַבֹּ֗שֶׁת אָֽכְלָ֛ה אֶת־ יְגִ֥יעַ אֲבוֹתֵ֖ינוּ מִנְּעוּרֵ֑ינוּ אֶת־ צֹאנָם֙ וְאֶת־ בְּקָרָ֔ם אֶת־ בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־ בְּנוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Let us lie down in our shame; let our disgrace cover us. We have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers; from our youth even to this day we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God.”
passages.sermon:
We feel deep shame.
Our disgrace covers us.
We have sinned against the LORD our God.
Our fathers have sinned against the LORD our God.
We have sinned since our youth.
Our fathers have sinned since their youth.
We have sinned until this day.
We have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God.
Our fathers have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God.
passages.original: נִשְׁכְּבָ֣ה בְּבָשְׁתֵּ֗נוּ וּֽתְכַסֵּנוּ֮ כְּלִמָּתֵנוּ֒ כִּי֩ לַיהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ חָטָ֗אנוּ אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ וַאֲבוֹתֵ֔ינוּ מִנְּעוּרֵ֖ינוּ וְעַד־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס
